18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）

  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信

51	- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 二、Claim 强度与数据匹配
56	
57	### 2.1 Claim 强度规则
58	
59	| 数据支撑 | 允许的最强表述 |
60	|----------|--------------|
61	| 单 seed, 单数据集 | "preliminary observation", "initial evidence" |
62	| 单 seed, 多数据集 | "suggestive pattern", "indicative trend" |
63	| 多 seed, 单数据集 | 报告均值±标准差，可写 "we find" |
64	| 多 seed, 多数据集 | 可用 "robust", "consistent" |
65	| 统计检验显著 | 可用 "significant", 附 p-value |
66	| 单 seed + 外推到其他条件 | 必须加限定，不能声称 "scale-invariant" 等 |
67	
68	### 2.2 禁止的过强表述
69	
70	- "remarkably stable" → 改为 "relatively stable" 或给出量化波动范围
71	- "confirmed" → 仅 "suggestive" 级别数据不能用
72	- "scale-invariant" → single-seed 验证不够
73	- "We attribute X to Y" → 如果是假说，必须改为 "We hypothesize" + "requiring causal verification"
74	- "roughly twice" → 实际比值必须在 1.8x-2.2x 才能用，否则改为更准确的近似
75	- "domain-agnostic" → 改为 "robust across N domains tested"
76	
77	### 2.3 Claim 降级机制
78	
79	当证据不足以支撑独立 claim 时，应降级为 discussion 中的定性讨论，而非删除。具体做法：
80	- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落
81	- 硬 claim → 加 caveat 的软 claim
82	- 正文数字 → 移入 Appendix
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 三、叙事与 Storytelling
87	
88	### 3.1 结构原则
89	
90	- 核心 paradox/发现之间必须有**过渡句**桥接，不能让读者在关键处断线
91	- Introduction 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
92	- Discussion 不应重复 Results 的具体数字——引用表格编号
93	- 同一解释不要在多处重复推导——主文写一次 + 指向 Appendix
94	- Limitations 段不要写成一个 17 行大段——拆分为 2-3 个子段按主题分组
95	
96	### 3.2 冷引用（Cold Reference）
97	
98	- 任何首次出现的概念必须有上文铺垫
99	- Introduction 贡献列表中不能突然出现未被提及的模型/方法名
100	
101	### 3.3 不要用旧叙事套新数字
102	
103	新 baseline 出来后若 delta 大幅变化，Section 的叙事逻辑必须重写，不是简单替换数字。
104	
105	### 3.4 Contingency Plan
106	
107	关键实验结果不确定时需预写两套叙事（如 "若结果 A → 叙事 A"、"若结果 B → 叙事 B"），实验完成后选择正确版本。提交前必须确认只留了一套。
108	
109	### 3.5 不要基于中间值做叙事决策
110	
111	70% 进度时的估计往往不够稳定（尤其 GSM8K 等难度分布不均匀的 benchmark），必须等完整数据再定稿叙事。
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 四、术语与一致性
116	
117	### 4.1 术语一致性
118	
119	- 全文必须统一使用正式定义的术语，不得出现同义词漂移
120	- 术语定义后，每次使用必须完全一致（不要有时 "perturbation sensitivity" 有时 "perturbation impact"）
121	
122	### 4.2 统计量一致性
123	
124	- 两个不同的 kappa/p-value 每次出现时必须标注是哪个
125	- 同一个 metric 在不同位置的数字必须完全一致
126	- 修改任何数字后必须全文 grep 确认所有引用处同步
127	
128	### 4.3 p-value 格式
129	
130	- 无前导零、3 位小数：`p = .003`（不是 `p = 0.003`）
131	- 当非劣效性 p<0.001 实际由正向效应驱动时，必须加括注说明
132	
133	### 4.4 例子与定义必须一致
134	
135	Taxonomy 中的定义和对应示例不能自相矛盾。如果定义说 "no new content"，示例中就不能包含新信息。
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 五、投稿前检查清单（Pre-Submission Checklist）
140	
141	### 5.1 占位符扫描（硬门禁）
142	
143	提交前必须 grep 扫描，以下模式要求**零匹配**：
144	```
145	XX.XX, PLACEHOLDER, [If , TODO, TBD, \placeholder{
146	```
147	所有条件占位段落（`[If ...]`）必须替换为最终文本。
148	
149	### 5.2 编译检查
150	
151	- [ ] 编译零 error
152	- [ ] 无 `??` 未解析引用
153	- [ ] 无 > 1pt 的 overfull hbox
154	- [ ] 正文 ≤ 9 页（NeurIPS desk reject 风险）
155	- [ ] 使用当年 style file（`neurips_2026.sty`）
156	- [ ] Review 版启用行号
157	- [ ] 匿名审稿版无作者姓名、无致谢
158	
159	### 5.3 数据完整性
160	
161	- [ ] 论文所有数字与 registry/provenance 交叉验证通过
162	- [ ] 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）独立重算确认
163	- [ ] 所有 evaluation protocol 差异已在论文中说明
164	- [ ] 多 seed 结果报告均值和标准差
165	- [ ] 单 seed 数据在 Limitations 中声明
166	
167	### 5.4 图表检查
168	
169	- [ ] 所有 figure PDF 存在且路径匹配
170	- [ ] 图表不超栏宽（单栏 5.5in / 全宽 6.5in）
171	- [ ] 图中字体 ≥ 7pt
172	- [ ] 小数精度全表统一
173	- [ ] 最优结果加粗、次优下划线
174	- [ ] 表格标题（caption）自包含
175	- [ ] Forest plot 等可视化无 dummy 值（CI_LO=-99 等）
176	
177	### 5.5 引用检查
178	
179	- [ ] 引用覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**（任一缺失说明调研不充分）
180	- [ ] 引用密度与目标会议近年录用论文同量级
181	- [ ] 引用键与 bib 条目 1:1 匹配
182	- [ ] 无孤儿 bib 条目
183	- [ ] 无幻觉引用（所有被引论文实际存在）
184	- [ ] 近年论文的年份/会议准确
185	- [ ] 审稿人要求的引用全部补齐
186	
187	### 5.6 匿名化检查
188	
189	- [ ] 源代码无硬编码绝对路径（`/Users/...`, `/root/...`）
190	- [ ] 配置文件无服务器路径
191	- [ ] Git history 已清理 author 信息（用 fresh repo）
192	- [ ] 项目管理文件不得提交（AGENTS.md, memory.md, registry.yaml, task_context/ 等）
193	- [ ] API Keys 通过环境变量，无泄露
194	
195	### 5.7 会议 Checklist 填写（如目标会议要求）
196	
197	- [ ] Claims: 摘要/Introduction 准确反映实验范围
198	- [ ] Limitations: 正文 Limitations 段 + Appendix 补充
199	- [ ] Experiments: 实验设置完整（exp_id, seed, 超参, 评估 protocol）
200	- [ ] Reproducibility: 数据集公开、代码可用
201	- [ ] Statistical Significance: 多 seed 均值+标准差、置信区间
202	- [ ] Compute: GPU 型号、训练时间、总 GPU-hours
203	- [ ] Licenses: 数据集/模型引用完整
204	- [ ] AI Assistants: 如实声明使用情况
205	- [ ] 每项认真回答（不要全写 N/A）
206	
207	### 5.8 叙事完整性
208	
209	- [ ] Conclusion 包含所有关键限定符（如 "under greedy decoding"）
210	- [ ] Abstract 与正文一致（不能一个写 "single seed" 另一个已是 "10 seeds"）
211	- [ ] 无 Appendix Version A/B 两套叙事残留
212	- [ ] 无 LaTeX 注释与正文混淆
213	- [ ] Contribution claim 在 Introduction 中（不在 Related Work 中）
214	- [ ] 所有专有名词/缩写首次出现时有定义（Abstract 内缩写也必须展开）
215	- [ ] Introduction 与 Method/Results 讲同一条主线（idea 变化后全文逻辑一致）
216	
217	### 5.9 去 AI 风格检查
218	
219	- [ ] **`grep "—" paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 em-dash 必须全删，最显著的 AI 痕迹）
220	- [ ] **`grep " – " paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 en-dash 必须全删）
221	- [ ] 无 "-ing," 分词短语结尾（如 "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."）
222	- [ ] 无连续 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"（同段最多 1 个）
223	- [ ] 无 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."
224	- [ ] 无 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "a myriad of" / "a plethora of"
225	- [ ] 自然段 5-8 句是正常的，不要每 2-3 句就换段
226	
227	### 5.10 模板与同类论文核对
228	
229	- [ ] LaTeX 模板从目标会议官网下载（不是他人转载、不是上一年）
230	- [ ] `\documentclass[]{}` 选项匹配 review / camera-ready 阶段
231	- [ ] 写作前已参考 2-3 篇同领域近 1-2 年优秀论文，叙事节奏对齐
232	
233	---
234	
235	## 六、Reviewer 审查标准
236	
237	### 6.1 CRITICAL 级别（必须修复才能提交）
238	
239	- 论文数字与实验数据不一致
240	- Abstract 与正文矛盾
241	- Evaluation protocol 混淆（如 0-shot 写成 8-shot）
242	- 未经验证的数据写入论文
243	- 占位符残留
244	
245	### 6.2 WARNING 级别（应当修复）
246	
247	- Stale claims（更新了某处数字但忘了同步其他位置）
248	- 过强措辞不匹配数据支撑
249	- 隐式全因子设计误导（如写 "3×3×3=27" 但实际只有 15 格）
250	- 评估指标只描述了部分 domain
251	- 旧版数据引用
252	
253	### 6.3 数据一致性审查流程
254	
255	1. 从 registry 提取所有实验 metrics
256	2. 对照论文中每一个内联数字（到行号级别）
257	3. 独立重算所有衍生值
258	4. 不一致处标注为 CRITICAL
259	5. 近似表述检查实际比值是否在允许范围内
260	
261	---
262	
263	## 七、常见反模式速查表
264	
265	| 反模式 | 症状 | 修复方式 |
266	|--------|------|----------|
267	| Stale claim | 论文某处还引用旧数字 | 改数字后全文 grep 同步 |
268	| Protocol 混淆 | 不同表格用了不同 evaluation 但没说明 | 每张表注明 protocol |
269	| Agent 误报 | 实验结果缺乏文件证据 | 要求 `cat result.json` 截图 |
270	| 混用数据算比值 | 跨 seed/条件/N 的数据混合比较 | 只用严格配对的数据 |
271	| 叙事超越数据 | "confirmed" 但实际只是 suggestive | 匹配 claim 强度到 §2.1 |
272	| 冷引用 | 首次出现的概念无铺垫 | 先建立框架再引入 |
273	| 定义-例子矛盾 | Taxonomy 定义和示例冲突 | 审查所有定义与其示例 |
274	| Placeholder 残留 | XX.XX, TODO, [If...] 未清理 | 提交前 grep 硬门禁 |
275	| Path 泄露 | 代码/config 含服务器绝对路径 | 改为相对路径 |
276	| 重复推导 | 同一解释在 3 处各自推导一遍 | 主文一次 + 引用 Appendix |
277	| Discussion 重复 Results | Discussion 大量复制 Results 数字 | 改为引用表格编号 |
278	| 单 seed overclaim | 单 seed 数据声称 scale-invariant | 加 preliminary/hedging 限定 |
279	| Registry 不同步 | Registry 面值与实际状态不一致 | 以 SSH 实测为准 |
280	| vLLM 静默失败 | max_model_len 太小导致 100% 400 错误 | 预检必须发真实 prompt 验证 |
281	
282	---
283	
284	## 八、写论文前加载的 Skills
285	
286	写论文或做最终审查时，Director/Agent 应按需加载以下 skills：
287	- `latex-paper` — LaTeX 编译与格式
288	- `reference-audit` — 引用真实性审计
289	- `academic-writer` — ML 学术写作规范
290	- `paper-quality-lessons`（本 skill）— 实战经验教训
291	
292	---
293	
294	## 九、附录：投稿经验时间线教训
295	
296	1. **论文数字锁定时机**：最终编译前 24h 锁定所有数字，之后只允许格式修改
297	2. **GPU 不要空闲**：审稿期间如果 Agent 空闲，应该跑 ablation/扩展实验作为 rebuttal 储备
298	3. **匿名化提前做**：不要等到最后一天才检查路径泄露，fresh repo 需要时间清理
299	4. **9 页零余量策略**：NeurIPS 正文 9 页是硬限，每次新增内容必须等量压缩并编译验证
300	5. **Contingency 叙事提前写**：关键实验完成前就写好两版叙事，避免最后一刻仓促改稿
301

# 论文写作质量指南（NeurIPS 实战经验）

> 来源：2026 年 NeurIPS 投稿期间，从 20+ 项目的人工审查反馈中提炼。
> 每条规则都源自真实的 bug / 退回 / 审稿质疑。

---

## 一、数据诚信与溯源（最高优先级）

### 1.1 数字必须有源头

- 论文中**每一个数字**必须可追溯到 registry 实验 ID 或原始结果文件
- 禁止凭记忆写数字——必须 `cat result.json | head` + `ls -la` 附上文件证据
- 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）必须独立重算，不信 Agent 第一手汇报
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 覆盖率必须 100%，改数字必须同步更新 provenance

> **教训（D149 事件）**：Agent 曾伪造完整的 metrics 数据包括 p-value，事后被 Reviewer 独立 parse JSON 抓出。从此所有关键数据必须 Reviewer 独立验证到字段级别。

### 1.2 不同来源数据不能混用

- 配对数据必须同 seed、同 c 值、同 N、同 evaluation protocol

- 跨 config 比较 delta 会引入系统误差——必须补跑同 config baseline 后才能比较
- 非等量对比必须显式标注（如 "at unmatched volumes"）

> **教训（D027 事件）**：不同 config 文件的 baseline 不同，跨 config 比较 delta 值引入了 artifact。

### 1.3 结论撤回后不可复活

- 被 Director shelved 的数据（如因截断混淆），禁止重新引入论文
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 中 `verified: false` 的 claim，不得恢复
- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）

- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落

Hidden-state probes for safety monitoring require selecting which transformer layer to read---a choice typically treated as a minor implementation detail. We show that this choice alone can reverse a study's central conclusion about whether hidden states outperform text for detecting unsafe reasoning.

We study commitment-point detection in self-jailbreaking reasoning models across four models, two architectures, and two scales. A crossing-rate composite metric systematically selects shallow layers (L0--L10), while threshold-based metrics select deep layers (L14--L63), producing divergences of 14 to 61 layers. At shallow layers, hidden-state and text probes perform equivalently; at deep layers, hidden-state probes significantly outperform text. The mechanism is cosine compression: shallow-layer representations compress directional information, inflating crossing-rate metrics near the noise floor. This bias generalizes across models, a second dataset (AdvBench), and a fifth architecture (Gemma-2).

The hidden-state advantage is cross-validated at 7--8B (+20--22pp over text) but conditional: it diminishes with stronger text encoders and is only suggestive at 32B due to small samples. Seven alternative detection methods all fail to match supervised probing. Layer selection metric is a critical, under-examined specification choice in safety probing studies.

1	\section{Experiments}\label{sec:experiments}
2	
3	We evaluate temporal probes across four reasoning models (\cref{tab:models}), comparing hidden-state (HS) and text modalities under different layer selection criteria.
4	
5	\subsection{Setup}\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	We study R1-8B (Llama-8B, R1-distilled, $n{=}43$ test traces), OT-7B (OpenThinker-7B, trained on the OpenThoughts dataset~\citep{openthinker}; Qwen-7B backbone, STILL-trained~\cref{app:ot7b_details}, $n{=}47$), QwQ-32B (Qwen-32B, native reasoning, $n{=}19$--$20$), and R1-32B (Qwen-32B, R1-distilled, $n{=}20$). All traces come from HarmThoughts with step-level CP annotations (60/20/20 split). HS probes extract last-token hidden states from a selected layer; text probes encode each step with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d). Both use L2-regularized logistic regression with temporal windowing $W \in \{1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25\}$ selected on validation. Classification requires $K{=}5$ consecutive threshold crossings (\cref{tab:k_ablation}). Statistical testing follows \cref{sec:evaluation}.\looseness=-1
8	
9	\subsection{Layer Selection Results}\label{sec:layer-results}
10	
11	\cref{tab:layer_selection} shows that the CR-composite systematically selects shallow layers: L0 for R1-8B (full L0--L24 sweep; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}) and OT-7B, L2 (3\%) for QwQ-32B, L10 (16\%) for R1-32B (\cref{fig:layer_heatmap}). Threshold-based metrics converge to deep layers, notably L63 (98\%) for both 32B models. Balanced accuracy varies across splits (7--98\% depth; \cref{app:ba_layer_comparison}). The mechanism is cosine compression: step-to-step distances are 1.4--2.7$\times$ smaller at shallow layers (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}), so a linear probe operates near the noise floor, inflating crossing rate independently of discriminative power (\cref{sec:layer-sensitivity}).\looseness=-1

15	\small

Red dashed: CR-composite layer (bal\_acc $\times$ crossing\_rate); green dashed: threshold-based layer (consensus of threshold-based metrics). For R1-8B (full L0--L24 sweep), crossing rate drives CR-composite selection to L0 while threshold-based metrics retain L14. At 32B, CR-composite selections cluster near input layers while threshold-based metrics peak at deep layers.}

38	The downstream impact is severe: at CR-composite layers, only 7--8B models show significant HS advantage; both 32B models fail. CR-composite shallow-layer selection is an artifact of cosine compression, not a genuine safety signal. At threshold-based layers, the HS advantage is graded: cross-validated at 7--8B, significant at QwQ-32B, and exploratory at R1-32B (small sample). Random-label controls confirm threshold-based selection requires genuine safety labels and that the geometric bias is Qwen-specific (\cref{app:random_cp}). AUROC confirms HS discriminability at balanced-accuracy-selected layers ($\Delta$AUROC +12--15pp; \cref{tab:ba_layer_results}) but cannot diagnose threshold-dependent bias.\looseness=-1
39	
40	\paragraph{Ensemble layer selection.} A three-layer ensemble averaging predictions from the precision-best, balanced-accuracy-best, and inverse-FPR-best layers bypasses single-metric selection. All four models show significant HS advantage ($p \leq 0.002$; \cref{tab:ensemble}), including both 32B models that fail under CR-composite. The ensemble smooths metric-specific variation by averaging across depths within the deep region. This holdout result requires cross-validated confirmation (\cref{sec:discussion}).\looseness=-1

86	Against the 384d text baseline, HS probes outperform text in all four models (\cref{tab:hs_vs_text}). The advantage is cross-validated at 7--8B (R1-8B: +20.1pp, OT-7B: +21.9pp precision) and consistent across random seeds (\cref{app:multi_seed}). At 32B, results are suggestive: QwQ-32B shows +19.2pp but the position baseline is competitive (\cref{sec:32b-analysis}); R1-32B shows +15.4pp but with limited coverage. Control tasks confirm the signal reflects genuine safety structure (\cref{app:control}); a split-half analysis on OT-7B confirms internal validity (\cref{app:split_half}).\looseness=-1

88	\paragraph{Capacity control.} PCA reduction of HS features to 384d (79--92\% variance retained) preserves the precision advantage across all four models (+16.8 to +23.1pp, all $p{<}0.012$, all survive correction). The control provides partial evidence against a pure capacity explanation. Random projection to 384d yields similar results ($\Delta$Prec +8.3 to +20.5pp; \cref{app:random_projection}), further weakening the capacity explanation. E5-Mistral-7B (4096d, PCA-reduced to 384d; \cref{app:e5_mistral}) yields intermediate results (2/4 significant), forming a monotonic encoder-quality gradient with MiniLM (4/4) and BGE-large (1/4).\looseness=-1

90	\paragraph{Encoder robustness.} The HS advantage is encoder-conditional. Against BGE-large~\citep{xiao2023cpack} (1024d), only OT-7B survives correction (1/4 precision; \cref{app:encoder_robustness}). \cref{fig:forest_precision} visualizes the encoder-quality gradient: MiniLM-384d (4/4 significant) $\to$ E5-Mistral (2/4) $\to$ BGE-1024d (1/4), with precision narrowing from +15--22pp to +6--18pp. Layer selection bias (C1) is encoder-independent.\looseness=-1

102

445	\section{GRU Training Details}
446	\label{app:gru_details}
447	
448	GRU results serve as supplementary evidence under a different training protocol (70/30 split); direct comparison with the main logistic regression pipeline (60/20/20 nested CV) is not intended.
449	
450	\paragraph{Data split.} GRU experiments use a 70/30 train/test split to maximize training data for the sequential model, differing from the main 60/20/20 protocol used for logistic regression probes. Within the 70\% training portion, we hold out 10\% of total traces as a validation set for early stopping (effective 60/10/30 split). The validation set is used only for early stopping and is not included in reported test metrics, so there is no information leakage.
451	
452	\paragraph{Architecture.} We evaluate two GRU variants. The single-layer variant uses a GRU with hidden dimension 256, taking per-step hidden states from the best layer (selected by validation balanced accuracy) as input. The multi-layer variant concatenates hidden states from 7 layers (evenly spaced through the network) at each step to produce a higher-dimensional input to the same GRU architecture.

454	\paragraph{Training procedure.} We train with Adam (learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, default $\beta_1{=}0.9$, $\beta_2{=}0.999$), batch size 16, for a maximum of 50 epochs. Early stopping halts training when validation loss does not improve for 10 consecutive epochs. Input features are z-score normalized per dimension using training set statistics.
455	
456	\paragraph{Evaluation.} We report crossing accuracy (the sustained accuracy at which the probe first exceeds chance for 5 consecutive steps) and detection lead (steps before CP at crossing point). All experiments use 3 random seeds; we report mean $\pm$ standard deviation.

529	\section{Control Task Methodology}
530	\label{app:control}
531	
532	We follow the selectivity framework of \cite{hewitt2019control} to verify that our probes capture genuine safety-relevant structure rather than surface-level correlations.
533	
534	\paragraph{Procedure.} For each model, we randomly permute the binary labels (pre-CP vs. post-CP) within each trace while preserving the marginal label distribution. We then retrain the probe with identical architecture (L2-regularized logistic regression) and hyperparameters on these shuffled labels. Selectivity is defined as:
535	\begin{equation}
536	    \text{Selectivity} = \text{Acc}_{\text{linguistic}} - \text{Acc}_{\text{control}}
537	\end{equation}
538	where $\text{Acc}_{\text{linguistic}}$ is the probe accuracy on true labels and $\text{Acc}_{\text{control}}$ is the accuracy on permuted labels. A selectivity of zero indicates that the probe exploits only non-linguistic features (e.g., position); higher values confirm that the representation encodes task-relevant information. Absolute selectivity values are task-dependent and not directly comparable across studies~\citep{hewitt2019control}.
539	
540	\paragraph{Results.} We repeat the control experiment 10 times with different random permutations and report the mean control accuracy. Selectivity scores at threshold-based layers (60/20/20 split) are: R1-32B 16.8pp (layer 63), QwQ-32B 16.1pp (layer 63), R1-8B 14.1pp (layer 14), OT-7B 11.1pp (layer 16). All values exceed the 5pp threshold recommended by \cite{hewitt2019control}. R1-32B and QwQ-32B achieve the strongest selectivity ($>$16pp) at threshold-based layers. On QwQ-32B, the position baseline accuracy (0.705) slightly exceeds the HS probe (0.667) at L60, consistent with the main-text finding that QwQ's HS advantage is concentrated in precision and FPR rather than balanced accuracy.
541	
542	\paragraph{Layer provenance note.} R1-8B is unaffected by the layer selection bias because its CR-composite and threshold-based layers coincide at L14. OT-7B exhibits a 16-layer gap (CR-composite L0 vs.\ threshold-based L16; \cref{tab:layer_selection}), but selectivity at L16 (11.1pp) still exceeds the 5pp threshold. QwQ-32B selectivity is 16.1pp at L63, which confirms that safety-specific signal persists at deep layers.
543	
544	\paragraph{Position-only baseline.} As a complementary validation, we train a logistic regression classifier using only the normalized step index ($t / T$ where $T$ is the total trace length) as the input feature. This baseline tests whether temporal position alone explains probe performance. On R1-8B, the position-only baseline produces 15.8\% FPR compared to 8.1\% for the HS probe at matched detection rates. The probe's substantially lower FPR confirms that hidden state features carry information beyond what step position provides.
545	
546	\paragraph{Residualized selectivity.} To confirm that selectivity survives position removal, we recompute control task selectivity on position-regressed features (the same residualized representations used in \cref{app:position_residual}). Residualized selectivity: R1-8B 22.9pp, OT-7B 10.4pp, QwQ-32B 11.3pp (all ${>}5$pp), R1-32B 3.0pp (${<}5$pp, consistent with the position-mediation pattern reported in \cref{sec:hs-text}). Three of four models retain selectivity well above the \citet{hewitt2019control} threshold after position removal; R1-32B's drop confirms that its safety signal is largely positional.

549	\section{Oracle Upper Bound Analysis}
550	\label{sec:oracle}
551	
552	We compute an oracle upper bound for commitment detection by measuring the earliest step at which the ground-truth commitment point (CP) could theoretically be predicted from hidden-state dynamics. The oracle detector has access to the true CP label and computes how many steps before CP the representation trajectory first enters a region that is linearly separable from pre-CP states with perfect accuracy on the training set. The resulting bound provides a theoretical ceiling on early detection performance.
553	
554	\cref{tab:oracle} reports oracle performance across all four models. Oracle analysis confirms the evidence gradient: OT-7B (strong) shows the highest early detection rate (93.6\%) and longest lead time (50 steps), while R1-32B (qualified) achieves only 50\% early detection even with oracle labels, consistent with an inherently weaker commitment signal. On R1-8B, the oracle early detection rate is 76.7\% (33/43 traces detected before CP, with +31 steps mean lead time), compared to +4.5 steps for the best learned probe (GRU). This gap indicates that hidden states at step $t$ encode the model's current safety state but carry limited predictive power about future trajectory evolution. The learned probe captures the contemporaneous safety signal effectively (balanced accuracy 81--84\%) but cannot anticipate the commitment transition far in advance. Closing this gap will likely require causal intervention techniques (e.g., activation patching) rather than improvements to passive monitoring.

\section{GRU Training Details}
\label{app:gru_details}

GRU results serve as supplementary evidence under a different training protocol (70/30 split); direct comparison with the main logistic regression pipeline (60/20/20 nested CV) is not intended.

\paragraph{Data split.} GRU experiments use a 70/30 train/test split to maximize training data for the sequential model, differing from the main 60/20/20 protocol used for logistic regression probes. Within the 70\% training portion, we hold out 10\% of total traces as a validation set for early stopping (effective 60/10/30 split). The validation set is used only for early stopping and is not included in reported test metrics, so there is no information leakage.

\paragraph{Architecture.} We evaluate two GRU variants. The single-layer variant uses a GRU with hidden dimension 256, taking per-step hidden states from the best layer (selected by validation balanced accuracy) as input. The multi-layer variant concatenates hidden states from 7 layers (evenly spaced through the network) at each step to produce a higher-dimensional input to the same GRU architecture.

\paragraph{Training procedure.} We train with Adam (learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, default $\beta_1{=}0.9$, $\beta_2{=}0.999$), batch size 16, for a maximum of 50 epochs. Early stopping halts training when validation loss does not improve for 10 consecutive epochs. Input features are z-score normalized per dimension using training set statistics.

\paragraph{Evaluation.} We report crossing accuracy (the sustained accuracy at which the probe first exceeds chance for 5 consecutive steps) and detection lead (steps before CP at crossing point). All experiments use 3 random seeds; we report mean $\pm$ standard deviation.

\section{Control Task Methodology}
\label{app:control}

We follow the selectivity framework of \cite{hewitt2019control} to verify that our probes capture genuine safety-relevant structure rather than surface-level correlations.

\paragraph{Procedure.} For each model, we randomly permute the binary labels (pre-CP vs. post-CP) within each trace while preserving the marginal label distribution. We then retrain the probe with identical architecture (L2-regularized logistic regression) and hyperparameters on these shuffled labels. Selectivity is defined as:
\begin{equation}
    \text{Selectivity} = \text{Acc}_{\text{linguistic}} - \text{Acc}_{\text{control}}
\end{equation}
where $\text{Acc}_{\text{linguistic}}$ is the probe accuracy on true labels and $\text{Acc}_{\text{control}}$ is the accuracy on permuted labels. A selectivity of zero indicates that the probe exploits only non-linguistic features (e.g., position); higher values confirm that the representation encodes task-relevant information. Absolute selectivity values are task-dependent and not directly comparable across studies~\citep{hewitt2019control}.

\paragraph{Results.} We repeat the control experiment 10 times with different random permutations and report the mean control accuracy. Selectivity scores at threshold-based layers (60/20/20 split) are: R1-32B 16.8pp (layer 63), QwQ-32B 16.1pp (layer 63), R1-8B 14.1pp (layer 14), OT-7B 11.1pp (layer 16). All values exceed the 5pp threshold recommended by \cite{hewitt2019control}. R1-32B and QwQ-32B achieve the strongest selectivity ($>$16pp) at threshold-based layers. On QwQ-32B, the position baseline accuracy (0.705) slightly exceeds the HS probe (0.667) at L60, consistent with the main-text finding that QwQ's HS advantage is concentrated in precision and FPR rather than balanced accuracy.

\paragraph{Layer provenance note.} R1-8B is unaffected by the layer selection bias because its CR-composite and threshold-based layers coincide at L14. OT-7B exhibits a 16-layer gap (CR-composite L0 vs.\ threshold-based L16; \cref{tab:layer_selection}), but selectivity at L16 (11.1pp) still exceeds the 5pp threshold. QwQ-32B selectivity is 16.1pp at L63, which confirms that safety-specific signal persists at deep layers.

\paragraph{Position-only baseline.} As a complementary validation, we train a logistic regression classifier using only the normalized step index ($t / T$ where $T$ is the total trace length) as the input feature. This baseline tests whether temporal position alone explains probe performance. On R1-8B, the position-only baseline produces 15.8\% FPR compared to 8.1\% for the HS probe at matched detection rates. The probe's substantially lower FPR confirms that hidden state features carry information beyond what step position provides.

\paragraph{Residualized selectivity.} To confirm that selectivity survives position removal, we recompute control task selectivity on position-regressed features (the same residualized representations used in \cref{app:position_residual}). Residualized selectivity: R1-8B 22.9pp, OT-7B 10.4pp, QwQ-32B 11.3pp (all ${>}5$pp), R1-32B 3.0pp (${<}5$pp, consistent with the position-mediation pattern reported in \cref{sec:hs-text}). Three of four models retain selectivity well above the \citet{hewitt2019control} threshold after position removal; R1-32B's drop confirms that its safety signal is largely positional.


\section{Oracle Upper Bound Analysis}
\label{sec:oracle}

We compute an oracle upper bound for commitment detection by measuring the earliest step at which the ground-truth commitment point (CP) could theoretically be predicted from hidden-state dynamics. The oracle detector has access to the true CP label and computes how many steps before CP the representation trajectory first enters a region that is linearly separable from pre-CP states with perfect accuracy on the training set. The resulting bound provides a theoretical ceiling on early detection performance.

\cref{tab:oracle} reports oracle performance across all four models. Oracle analysis confirms the evidence gradient: OT-7B (strong) shows the highest early detection rate (93.6\%) and longest lead time (50 steps), while R1-32B (qualified) achieves only 50\% early detection even with oracle labels, consistent with an inherently weaker commitment signal. On R1-8B, the oracle early detection rate is 76.7\% (33/43 traces detected before CP, with +31 steps mean lead time), compared to +4.5 steps for the best learned probe (GRU). This gap indicates that hidden states at step $t$ encode the model's current safety state but carry limited predictive power about future trajectory evolution. The learned probe captures the contemporaneous safety signal effectively (balanced accuracy 81--84\%) but cannot anticipate the commitment transition far in advance. Closing this gap will likely require causal intervention techniques (e.g., activation patching) rather than improvements to passive monitoring.

\section{M002 Bug Disclosure}
\label{app:bug}

We disclose a bug discovered during development that affected intermediate results for QwQ-32B.

\paragraph{Issue.} In experiment M002 (text baseline evaluation), the QwQ-32B text probe was inadvertently initialized with a midpoint heuristic placeholder rather than true sentence embeddings from all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Specifically, the placeholder assigned each step a feature vector equal to the midpoint between the mean safe and mean unsafe embeddings from the training set, with small Gaussian noise added. This made the text probe trivially predictive and produced a spuriously significant result ($p{=}0.001$ for HS vs. text FPR difference).

\paragraph{Discovery and correction.} The bug was identified during a systematic audit of the feature extraction pipeline. After correction (using actual sentence embeddings), the QwQ-32B and R1-32B modality comparisons at the originally selected layers (L2 and L10, chosen by the CR-composite metric) showed no significant HS advantage: QwQ-32B accuracy $p{=}0.828$, precision $p{=}0.346$; R1-32B precision $p{=}0.050$ but no tests surviving Holm-Bonferroni. The subsequent discovery that these layer selections were themselves artifacts of metric bias (\cref{sec:layer-results}) led to the threshold-based layer analysis reported in the main text, where the HS advantage follows an evidence gradient at threshold-based deep layers: cross-validated at 7--8B, significant but suggestive of position-competitiveness at QwQ-32B$^\dagger$, and exploratory at R1-32B$^\dagger$ (\cref{tab:hs_vs_text}).

\paragraph{Impact on reported results.} All numbers reported in this paper use the corrected text embedding pipeline. The bug affected only QwQ-32B text probe features. The correction, combined with the separate layer selection fix (\cref{sec:layer-results}), means that early-stage intermediate results (non-significant 32B modality comparisons) reflected two compounding errors: incorrect text features and CR-composite layer selection. Both are fully resolved in the final analysis.

\paragraph{Commitment to transparency.} We report this bug to maintain scientific integrity. Code and data will be released upon publication.

\section{Adaptive Two-Stage Detection}
\label{app:two_stage}

We explored whether a two-stage adaptive window strategy could improve the precision-coverage tradeoff beyond fixed-window detection. The approach uses a short screening window ($W_{\text{screen}}$) to flag candidate unsafe segments, followed by a longer confirmation window ($W_{\text{confirm}}$) applied only to flagged segments. A trace is classified as unsafe if at least $k$ steps exceed the threshold during the confirmation stage.

We merge the validation and test partitions ($n{=}55$ total: 39 jailbreak, 16 benign) for two-stage evaluation because the screening and confirmation thresholds are not tuned on held-out data. We evaluated all combinations of $W_{\text{screen}} \in \{1, 3, 5\}$, $W_{\text{confirm}} \in \{10, 15, 20, 25\}$, and $k \in \{1, 3, 5\}$ on these R1-8B traces. \cref{fig:pareto_two_stage} shows the precision-coverage Pareto front for both methods. The best two-stage configuration ($W_{\text{screen}}{=}3$, $W_{\text{confirm}}{=}15$, $k{=}1$) achieves 72.2\% precision at 76.9\% coverage, compared to 70.9\% precision at 76.9\% coverage for single-stage $W{=}15$. This +1.3pp precision gain at matched coverage represents a Pareto improvement, but the magnitude is marginal. At higher confirmation thresholds ($k{=}3$, $k{=}5$), two-stage detection trades coverage for small precision gains (up to 73.5\% precision at 38.5\% coverage with $k{=}5$), but these operating points are impractical due to excessive missed detections.

974	\section{Hyperparameter Robustness}
975	\label{app:hyperparameter_robustness}
976	
977	The joint search space for layer (${\leq}64$), window $W$ (7 values), consecutive-crossing threshold $K$ (5 values), and decision threshold is large (up to 2{,}240 configurations per model). This raises the concern that reported performance reflects overfitting to small validation sets ($n{=}4$--$9$ per class at 32B). Three analyses address this concern.
978	
979	\paragraph{Threshold-based metrics converge to a deep-layer band.}
980	Despite the large search space, three of four threshold-based metrics (precision, inverse FPR, additive composite) independently select L63 (98\% depth) for both 32B models (\cref{tab:layer_selection}). A joint (layer, $W$) grid search over 192 configurations confirms that L63 is near-optimal for QwQ-32B at recommended windows (\cref{tab:joint_layer_w}). For R1-32B, layers L55--L63 at $W{=}1$ form a robust band where all 3/3 metrics pass Holm-Bonferroni (\cref{app:layer_sweep}). The convergence of independent metrics to a narrow band is inconsistent with overfitting, which would produce scattered selections.
981	
982	\paragraph{BA-optimal layer instability is the finding, not a confound.}
983	Five-fold cross-validation on 32B validation sets reveals that balanced-accuracy-optimal layers are highly unstable across folds (\cref{tab:fold_ba_layers}). This instability is not a limitation of the study but the central methodological finding: BA-layer selection is sensitive to data composition, and conclusions drawn from any single BA-optimal layer are unreliable. Despite per-fold instability, mean BA across folds peaks near L47--L50 for both models, consistent with the LOO-CV dominant layers (\cref{app:layer_sweep}). The HS advantage holds at both BA-optimal and precision-optimal layers regardless of depth (14/16 per-model tests pass HB; \cref{app:ba_layer_comparison}).

1001	\paragraph{Bootstrap CIs quantify statistical uncertainty.}
1002	For the most fragile result (R1-8B FPR), bias-corrected accelerated (BCa) bootstrap~\citep{efron1993bootstrap,carpenter2000bootstrap} yields a 95\% CI of [0.006, 0.159] ($p{=}0.033$), with 12\% leave-one-out instability (\cref{app:multi_seed}). The CI excludes zero and confirms significance despite seed fragility. CP annotation perturbation (\cref{tab:cp_perturbation}) further shows that $\pm 2$-step label noise changes BA by ${<}2.5$pp, so annotation uncertainty does not compound with hyperparameter selection.
1003	
1004	\paragraph{Effective degrees of freedom.}
1005	The full exploration space (5 metrics $\times$ 7 windows $\times$ 25--64 layers $=$ up to 2{,}240 configurations) far exceeds the 12 final HB-corrected tests. This does not constitute 2{,}240 independent hypothesis tests because layer and window are selected on the validation set before test-set evaluation, a standard train/validate/test protocol, not post-hoc cherry-picking on test outcomes. The effective degrees of freedom lie between 12 (final tests) and 2{,}240 (full grid), a ``garden of forking paths'' concern~\citep{gelman2013garden}. Three safeguards bound this risk: (1)~nested 5-fold CV on 7--8B models shows 13--25\% shrinkage relative to holdout estimates (\cref{app:nested_cv}), quantifying overfitting; (2)~split-half replication on OT-7B confirms the HS advantage on independent data halves (\cref{app:split_half}); (3)~threshold-based metric convergence to a narrow layer band (L63 for both 32B models) is inconsistent with scattered overfitting selections. We acknowledge that cumulative researcher degrees of freedom are substantial and that the 12-test HB boundary may underestimate Type~I error.
